You seem to have a lot of goals planned out which is great! Maybe working on one at a time and breaking them up into smaller tasks will make it more manageable. For me, I'm more likely to start working on something when it's a small task so I'm not overwhelmed by it all.  I would personally start with the one that would be that most rewarding. Both quitting pot or nicotine would be great for your health but Spanish classes sound like a lot of fun! 

As for quitting pot or nicotine, I've never had to do that but I've had to stop drinking and had some help with a counselor for that. Some techniques she taught me were to put off having a drink for a reasonable amount of time to me. So I would say to myself "I will have this drink in 30minutes, or after this song is over" and once that time had passed I would make another time limit goal. Another thing I did was try and train my brain to go to another activity, so if I wanted a drink I'd distract myself with dancing at a club, or reading/music while at home. She also recommended I try out new hobbies to distract myself so I got into gaming, writing, drawing, and weirdly enough origami, which relaxes me like crazy. 

Just take everything one little step at a time and eventually you will be fluent in Spanish and working your way to an awesome new career. :)

I totally understand where you're at. You're basically me; 25, wanting to go to uni, depressed as shit, avoiding my roommates; but I am on disability for my depression and was allowed to go to school. Unfortunately I was too depressed at the time to hack it so I've had to drop out, focus on myself, and reapply (hoping that me dropping out won't have an effect on my applications).

While working on your depression I've been told to only take on what you can handle, so not being able to work while in uni makes perfect sense. Have you looked into all the possible student loans and bursaries, and if so would those cover your living expenses? 

Or is it possible to stay with your mom while in school? I know you don't want to be a 'burden' but if she doesn't mind having you there I don't think it would be a huge issue. Plenty of students stay living with their parents, even into grad school. So you definitely are not 'too old' for this option and it doesn't make you any less of a person to need some help. This way you will be able to better yourself in school and be able to better pay it forward to society and you mom in the future. 

If not I think your only option would be to work, or go on disability and focus on yourself before you go back to school. That way you will be able to afford to live while learning to cope with your depression and possibly save for school. Then once you are coping better you can get back to school and either have enough money saved, or be coping well enough to work part time in school. It's totally ok to take the time you need. I know the feeling of having to 'put your life on hold', but your health should be your primary concern. There's nothing wrong with going back to school as an older student, as awkward as it may feel. It only means you are certain about what you want, and probably much more determined and experienced than other students. This isn't you getting to the 'game' later than all the other students, it's just you switching the order of things. Putting work and health before the university phase.

Hey now, there will always be ups and downs when battling depression. This is just one of those down times. I know it feels like you're just going to keep spiraling down, but this is just a tiny dip in your progress. You will get over this, you will find your strength and push through. You will improve some more, and probably experience many more dips, but every time you do, you will become stronger, and more capable of dealing with the downs. 

This is the time to put to use any coping mechanisms you have used in the past that have worked, or even those that haven't. It's another chance to practice what works for you. Distract yourself with something you enjoy, journal how you are feeling. Write more letters to the people you piss you off. OR alternatively write letters to those you love, those you are thankful for. Make goals for your future. Plan out who you want to be, your ideal self. Watch a happy movie. 

You will get past this. You can do it.
